subtopic: Money attitudes, family finances, gifting, borrowing between relatives
passage:
I'm Ishita, and I share a wall with Neelam's flat. In March Neelam's uncle bought her a costly scooter for the new job, and she was delighted, taking the whole floor for a ride. By June he had begun phoning. One evening I heard through the wall: "Uncle, thank you again for the scooter. I will always be grateful. I can drive your daughter to coaching on Saturdays, but not every evening."
Then quiet. I don't know what Neelam felt. But the next week the scooter was in the parking lot as usual, and Neelam still went to the evening class every Tuesday. The uncle's number came up on the screen a few more times, and the tone at the door was polite.

qa.q: In which month did Neelam's uncle buy the scooter?
qa.a: He bought the scooter in March.

qa.q: What might Neelam have felt when the uncle's calls began in June?
qa.a: Neelam may have felt pressured or uneasy, though the narrator says they cannot know for sure what Neelam felt.

qa.q: What choice did Neelam make on the phone that kept the relationship clean?
qa.a: Neelam thanked the uncle again, offered to drive his daughter to coaching on Saturdays, and declined every evening, so the gift did not become control.

qa.q: How might Ishita's view of Neelam's call differ from Neelam's own experience?
qa.a: Ishita only heard through the wall and cannot know Neelam's feelings, so Ishita sees the polite refusal but not what it cost Neelam.

grounding: A young adult gets a costly gift from a relative that later becomes a reason for favours, and accepts kindly while keeping freedom.

passage:
Monday: Joseph Uncle placed a boxed laptop on the table. "For your new job, Yamini." She hugged him, thrilled.
Friday: On the phone he said, "After all I've done for you, you'll do the accounts for my shop every weekend, won't you?" Yamini's chest tightened and she said she would think.
Wednesday: She rang him. "Uncle, I love the laptop and I thank you again. My weekends are not free. But I can help on an occasional Sunday if you ask me ahead." He was silent, then said, "Fine. Ask your aunt for the tea." She could hear it wasn't quite fine, but the line stayed warm.

qa.q: What did Joseph Uncle give Yamini on Monday?
qa.a: He gave Yamini a boxed laptop.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling when Joseph Uncle said 'After all I've done for you'?
qa.a: She felt her chest tighten with pressure and unease, as the gift suddenly seemed to carry a debt.

qa.q: What choice did Yamini make on Wednesday, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She thanked him again, kept her weekends free and offered an occasional Sunday by request, so she was kind without giving away her freedom.

qa.q: How might Joseph Uncle have felt when Yamini said her weekends were not free?
qa.a: He was probably disappointed, since he went silent and said 'Fine', but his reply about the tea suggests he still wanted to keep things warm.

grounding: A young adult receives a costly gift that turns into a claim for favours, and keeps freedom while thanking kindly.
